source_text.body:
Build and deploy a project end to end with Copilot CLI
The poster built a project with Copilot and used Copilot CLI to deploy and set up the website, saying it beat Claude Code for their workflow.
·
Mar 1, 2026
Done with
GH
GitHub Copilot
CC
Claude Code
What they did
The poster says they used Copilot to build an AI-agent marketplace, with OpenClaw managing the work while they remoted into VS Code and watched. Copilot generated Mongoose schemas and CRUD routes, React components with shadcn/ui, Next.js App Router handlers, and repeated patterns like validation, error handling, and auth middleware; they say Copilot CLI handled deployment and site setup, while they leaned on Claude Code only for harder escrow, contract, analytics, and debugging logic.
How it went
The result was a live site built on Next.js 14, MongoDB Atlas, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, PM2, and an AWS EC2 t3.small instance, plus SOL, ETH, and USDC payments. The poster’s main limitation was that complex state-machine and multi-party business logic still needed extra help.
Worth knowing
The only concrete operating cost given is AWS EC2 t3.small at about $15 per month.
Try it yourself
with
GitHub Copilot
Copy prompt
Help me deploy my project in [path or repo] to [hosting provider] using Copilot CLI. Walk through the setup of the server, domain and environment variables for [site or app name]. Before you run any command that changes remote infrastructure, spends money, or deletes anything, show me the exact command and wait for my OK. Finish with a live URL and a checklist of what was configured.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/GithubCopilot/comments/1rqoi7a/i_think_copilot_is_now_better_than_cursor_copilot
